correctness.rationale: Tang's full paper was inspected through Section 4.2. Fourier inversion shows that for a Hamming-distance-one pair all modes with j_c=0 cancel, and maximizing the real pole order forces every unchanged coordinate index to zero. For l_c=2 the unique dominant pole has order 1-2/m and positive Selberg-Delange constant, giving an eventual fixed sign. For l_c>=3 the dominant conjugate pair has nonzero amplitude and frequency sin(2pi/l_c)/m, giving infinitely many sign changes. In the explicit M=5, l=(3,2,1,1) example the surviving pole orders are 1/2 and 1/8 plus/minus i sqrt(3)/8, so the x/sqrt(log x) binary bias dominates.
